claims.claim: **Most cyanotic episodes in children with CHD are self-limiting.**
claims.source_text: Most cyanotic episodes in children with congenital heart disease (CHD) are self-limiting
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cyanotic episodes in congenital heart disease' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cyanotic_episodes_in_congenital_heart_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Let the parent comfort the child**; clinicians use a **minimal handling** approach with a targeted examination.
claims.source_text: The child should be comforted by the parent, clinicians should use a minimal handling approach with targeted examination
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cyanotic episodes in congenital heart disease' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cyanotic_episodes_in_congenital_heart_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Prolonged episodes may be life-threatening** and need active treatment with **oxygen and opiates**; involve senior staff and specialists early.
claims.source_text: Prolonged episodes may be life threatening and require active treatment with oxygen and opiates … Early involvement of senior staff and specialist advice is important in prolonged episodes
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cyanotic episodes in congenital heart disease' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cyanotic_episodes_in_congenital_heart_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **A cyanotic ('tet') spell** is acute cyanosis, or cyanosis worse than the child's baseline — most often in **Tetralogy of Fallot and pulmonary atresia**.
claims.source_text: Cyanotic episodes in children with congenital heart disease (also known as hypercyanotic spells, hypoxic spells or “tet spells”) are acute episodes of cyanosis or exaggerated cyanosis compared to the child’s baseline. They most often occur in children with Tetralogy of Fallot and pulmonary atresia
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cyanotic episodes in congenital heart disease' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cyanotic_episodes_in_congenital_heart_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Mechanism:** a pulmonary–systemic vascular resistance imbalance reduces pulmonary flow and increases right-to-left shunting.
claims.source_text: Cyanotic episodes are due to an imbalance between pulmonary and systemic vascular resistance with decreased pulmonary flow, and increased right to left shunting of blood
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cyanotic episodes in congenital heart disease' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cyanotic_episodes_in_congenital_heart_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Peak age 2–6 months**; usually triggered by stress — infection, being upset, or on waking.
claims.source_text: Most commonly occur between 2-6 months of age … Usually occur during times of stress, for example when unwell with an infection, when upset or upon waking
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cyanotic episodes in congenital heart disease' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cyanotic_episodes_in_congenital_heart_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **History:** known structural heart disease, **severe cyanosis (more than usual), hyperpnoea**, precipitants (distress, prolonged crying, dehydration, intercurrent illness), lethargy or altered conscious state; older children may have a history of **squatting**.
claims.source_text: Known history or evidence of structural heart disease Severe cyanosis (more than usual) Hyperpnoea Precipitating factors eg distress, prolonged crying, dehydration, intercurrent illness Lethargy, altered conscious state In older children, there may be a history of squatting episodes
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cyanotic episodes in congenital heart disease' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cyanotic_episodes_in_congenital_heart_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Examine gently and briefly** so as not to distress the child: compare cyanosis with baseline on **oxygen saturation monitoring**, assess hydration and perfusion, auscultate for a murmur if able.
claims.source_text: Minimal handling approach with limited and gentle examination to avoid distressing child Degree of cyanosis compared to baseline – apply oxygen saturation monitoring Assess hydration and perfusion Auscultate for murmur if able
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cyanotic episodes in congenital heart disease' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cyanotic_episodes_in_congenital_heart_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Calm the child — distress can worsen or prolong the spell.** Keep handling minimal and the child with the parent as much as possible.
claims.source_text: Aim to calm the child because distress can worsen or prolong cyanotic episodes … Minimal handling approach, child remaining with parent as much as possible
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cyanotic episodes in congenital heart disease' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cyanotic_episodes_in_congenital_heart_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Place the child in the knee-to-chest position** (lying supine or held upright) to increase systemic vascular resistance.
claims.source_text: Place child in knee to chest position to increase systemic vascular resistance … Knee to chest position lying supine Knee to chest position held upright
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cyanotic episodes in congenital heart disease' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cyanotic_episodes_in_congenital_heart_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Investigate after the spell has resolved**, guided by likely precipitants; an **ECG helps exclude an arrhythmia**.
claims.source_text: Consider performing after episode has resolved to avoid distressing child Guided by possible precipitating factors … An ECG is also helpful in excluding an arrhythmia
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cyanotic episodes in congenital heart disease' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cyanotic_episodes_in_congenital_heart_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Monitor until the spells have resolved and the child is not sedated from opiates.** Discuss ongoing observation and management with Cardiology.
claims.source_text: Monitor to ensure resolution of cyanotic episodes, and that child is not sedated due to opiate administration … Discuss with Cardiology regarding ongoing observation and management
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cyanotic episodes in congenital heart disease' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cyanotic_episodes_in_congenital_heart_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consult the local paediatric team** for any spell needing treatment; **consider transfer** if ICU admission or Cardiology review is needed.
claims.source_text: Consider consultation with local paediatric team when Child present with cyanotic spells requiring treatment … Consider transfer when Child requiring ICU admission or review by Cardiology
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cyanotic episodes in congenital heart disease' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cyanotic_episodes_in_congenital_heart_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consider discharge when** the child is back to baseline, not sedated, and Cardiology has been consulted.
claims.source_text: Consider discharge when The child is back to baseline, not sedated and consultation with Cardiology has occurred
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Cyanotic episodes in congenital heart disease' (Last updated November 2022), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Cyanotic_episodes_in_congenital_heart_disease/, retrieved 2026-09-23
